caption:
5 Balinese words to learn before you land. Save this for your trip.

05 Om Swastiastu: hello, and a small blessing
04 Suksma: thank you
03 Canang sari: the little daily offerings
02 Banjar: the village community
01 Bingin: the banyan tree

Number 1 is also our corner of the Bukit, home to Yume by Nyara: three private-pool villas on the cliffs. Link in bio to book your stay in Bali.

slides.sub: Number 1 is the name of our corner of the island.

slides.label: 05 · Om Swastiastu
slides.body: A greeting and a small blessing in one, from Sanskrit for “may it be well”. Say it om swah-stee-AH-stoo.

slides.label: 04 · Suksma
slides.body: Say it SOOK-smuh, or matur suksma to be extra polite. Terima kasih works all over Indonesia, but suksma is Bali's own.

slides.label: 03 · Canang sari
slides.body: Sari means “essence”. The flowers face the four directions: white east, red south, yellow west, blue or green north.

slides.label: 02 · Banjar
slides.body: Every Balinese neighbourhood has one: a community that organises ceremonies, cares for temples and meets at its bale banjar hall.

slides.label: 01 · Bingin
slides.body: Bingin is the Balinese word for the banyan, a holy tree often wrapped in black-and-white cloth. It's also our clifftop on the Bukit.

slides.credit: Villa Dua, Yume by Nyara, Bingin
slides.eyebrow: Now say it with us: suksma
slides.body: Three private-pool villas above Bingin, each with its own gate and garden. From USD 135 a night.
